answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive guide to the medicines you can take when you get a cold, organized by symptom:

---

> ⚠️ **Disclaimer:** This is general information only. Always consult your doctor or pharmacist before taking any medication, especially if you have existing health conditions or take other medications.

---

## 🤧 General Overview

There's still no cure for the common cold. Cold medicines seek to relieve symptoms rather than cure the illness or make it go away faster. Generally, over-the-counter medicine may help you feel better, but remember that these medications only treat the symptoms, not the illness itself. Only time and rest will help your immune system fight off a common cold.

---

## 💊 Medicines by Symptom

### 1. 🤒 Fever, Headache & Body Aches (Pain Relievers)
Pain relievers can help reduce a fever, ease headaches, and soothe body aches. Common options include:
- **Ibuprofen (Advil)** – a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that can also help reduce inflammation.
- **Naproxen (Aleve)** – another NSAID that can be dosed less frequently throughout the day.
- **Acetaminophen (Tylenol)** – works as a fever reducer and pain reliever, and may be an option for patients who shouldn't take NSAIDs due to heart or kidney disease.

### 2. 👃 Stuffy Nose (Decongestants)
The best medicines for a stuffy nose are decongestants. They help open nasal passageways by reducing swelling. Active ingredients to look for include pseudoephedrine (in pills or liquid), phenylephrine (in nasal sprays), and oxymetazoline (in nasal sprays).

However, decongestants help reduce swelling by restricting blood vessels, so they may not be appropriate for people with high blood pressure. Talk with your doctor before taking them.

### 3. 🤧 Runny Nose (Antihistamines)
A runny nose, watery eyes, and sneezing can be caused by histamines — chemicals your body produces. Medications that contain antihistamines can help block their release and clear up symptoms. One example is diphenhydramine (Benadryl).

Be aware that first-generation antihistamines may be more effective for colds, but also have the potential for excessive drowsiness.

### 4. 😮 Cough (Cough Suppressants & Expectorants)
Look for cough medicine that contains **dextromethorphan** (to suppress a dry cough) or **guaifenesin** (to break up mucus related to a wet cough).

Some medications that contain dextromethorphan also contain guaifenesin, an expectorant that thins out mucus and helps your cough to be "productive," meaning you're coughing out mucus that could be aggravating your throat and chest.

### 5. 😴 Nighttime Relief
Cold medicines designed for daytime use may include stimulating ingredients, such as a decongestant, while nighttime medications may include medications that cause drowsiness, like some antihistamines. For restful nighttime sleep, check ingredients in the medicine you've chosen to make sure they won't keep you awake.

---

## ⚠️ Important Safety Tips

- Since most cold medications treat more than one symptom, it can be helpful to identify your most severe symptom and make your choice based on lessening that symptom. It's important not to take two medications that contain the same active ingredients, as you may get too much of the drug in your system, leading to more side effects or serious health problems.

- Don't ask your healthcare professional for **antibiotics** for a cold. You won't get well faster, and using antibiotics when you don't need them adds to the serious and growing problem of antibiotic-resistant germs.

- Cold and cough medicine can harm children. Do **not** give any cough and cold medicines to children under age 4 years.

- Do **not** give children or teenagers aspirin, as it has been linked to Reye's syndrome, a rare life-threatening condition.

---

## 🏠 General Self-Care Tips

- Along with medication, get lots of rest so your body can fight the cold, and stay well hydrated. The more fluids you drink, the more the mucus is thinned out and you're able to get it out of the body quicker.
- Try sipping hot liquids like chicken soup, warm apple juice, or hot tea with honey to soothe a sore throat and relieve congestion.
- Saline (in the form of nose drops, spray, or neti pot) can help irrigate your nose, relieving nasal congestion and stuffiness.

---

Remember, consult your doctor or pharmacist — they can help you choose the best medicine for your symptoms.
